title: The Real Reason the French Love Protesting (Understand Native English & Culture)

subtitles.en:
Hello, everyone! Welcome back, to our slow
English podcast.
subtitles.zh: 大家哈囉！歡迎回到我們的慢速英語節目。

subtitles.en:
I am Alex, and this is Mia. Today, we have, a
crazy story, for you.
subtitles.zh:
我是 Alex，這位是 Mia。今天，我們要和大家分享一個非常不可思議
的故事。

subtitles.en:
Alex, have you seen, the viral clips, from
Paris, lately?
subtitles.zh: Alex，你最近有看到網路上瘋傳的巴黎短片嗎？

subtitles.en: Yes, I have! The streets, look totally wild.
subtitles.zh: 有啊！街頭看起來整個陷入一片混亂。

subtitles.en:
Streets blocked, with thick smoke, and crowds
shouting, everywhere.
subtitles.zh: 街道被濃煙封鎖，到處都能聽見群眾激動的抗議呼喊。

subtitles.en: And guess what, triggered, this whole mess?
subtitles.zh: 而且你猜猜看，究竟是什麼引爆了這整場混亂？

subtitles.en: A new law? Or, higher taxes?
subtitles.zh: 是頒布了新法律？還是政府又調高稅收了？

subtitles.en:
Nope! A local high school, simply did not
have, enough teachers.
subtitles.zh: 都不是！單純只是一所當地高中，找不到足夠的老師而已。

subtitles.en: Wait, what? A teacher shortage?
subtitles.zh: 等等，什麼？只是因為學校缺老師？

subtitles.en: Exactly. Just, missing teachers.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯，純粹只是老師人手不夠。

subtitles.en:
How does, a missing teacher, set the whole
country, on fire?
subtitles.zh: 缺幾位老師，怎麼會讓整個國家都陷入怒火與動盪？

subtitles.en:
Well, that was just the spark, that started,
everything.
subtitles.zh: 因為那只是點燃這一切的一顆小火星。

subtitles.en:
The spark? That sounds, like a great English
phrase!
subtitles.zh: 火星？這聽起來是個很棒的英文表達方式呢！

subtitles.en:
It is! Our first expression today, is: Spark,
a chain reaction.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯！我們今天的第一個核心片語就是：引發連鎖反應。

subtitles.en:
Spark... a chain... reaction! Let us say
that, slowly.
subtitles.zh: 引發……連鎖……反應！讓我們放慢速度，一起念一遍。

subtitles.en:
Spark, means to ignite, or trigger something,
suddenly.
subtitles.zh: 這個字當動詞使用時，意思是點燃、或是突然觸發某件事情。

subtitles.en: Like striking a match, in a dark room!
subtitles.zh: 就像在漆黑的房間裡，擦亮了一根小火柴！

subtitles.en:
Exactly. And a chain reaction, is a series,
of connected events.
subtitles.zh: 完全正確。而連鎖反應，則是指一連串相互關聯、接踵而來的事件。

subtitles.en:
Like falling dominoes! Push one, and they
all, collapse.
subtitles.zh: 就像骨牌一樣！推倒第一張，後面的就全部跟著倒下了。

subtitles.en:
Precisely. At first, the students, walked out
of class, to protest.
subtitles.zh: 太貼切了。最初，只是學生走出教室發起罷課抗議。

subtitles.en:
Because, they had no one, to teach them math,
or French.
subtitles.zh: 因為他們連數學課和法語課，都沒有老師來上課。

subtitles.en:
Right. But within days, other schools, joined
in.
subtitles.zh: 對啊。但不出幾天，其他學校也紛紛響應加入。

subtitles.en: Then, university students, joined too, right?
subtitles.zh: 接著連大學生也跟著站出來了，對吧？

subtitles.en:
Yes. And then, labor unions, stepped into the
streets.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯。最後連各大工會團體也紛紛走上街頭聲援。

subtitles.en:
So, a small shortage, sparked, a national
crisis!
subtitles.zh: 所以一個小小的人力短缺，竟然引爆了全國性的重大危機！

subtitles.en:
Yes. You can say: One mistake, sparked, a
chain reaction.
subtitles.zh: 是的。在生活中你可以說：一個小小的疏失，引發了一連串的連鎖反應。

subtitles.en:
Alex, peaceful protests, happen all the time,
in France.
subtitles.zh: Alex，在法國，和平抗議本來就滿常見的吧。

subtitles.en:
True. It is almost, like a national, weekend
sport!
subtitles.zh: 確實。抗議在法國簡直就像每週末的國民運動一樣！

subtitles.en: So, why did this protest, turn, so violent?
subtitles.zh: 那為什麼這一次的抗爭，會演變成如此劇烈的衝突呢？

subtitles.en:
Because, public frustration, was already, at
a boiling point.
subtitles.zh: 因為大眾內心的不滿與委屈，早就已經達到沸點邊緣了。

subtitles.en:
At a boiling point? Like water, on a hot
stove?
subtitles.zh: 達到沸點？就像爐子上燒滾的熱水一樣嗎？

subtitles.en:
Yes! When water boils, steam builds up,
intense pressure.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯！水沸騰的時候，蒸氣會累積出巨大的壓力。

subtitles.en:
If you do not turn down the heat, the pot,
boils over!
subtitles.zh: 如果不把火關小，整個鍋子裡的水就會滾沸溢出來！

subtitles.en:
Exactly. Living costs, in France, have been
rising, sharply.
subtitles.zh: 完全沒錯。法國的生活成本最近幾年飆漲得太厲害了。

subtitles.en:
Groceries, electricity, rent... everything,
is getting more expensive.
subtitles.zh: 食材採買、電費、房租……樣樣東西都在變貴。

subtitles.en:
People felt unheard, so their anger, boiled
over.
subtitles.zh: 民眾覺得自己的心聲沒有被聽見，積壓的怒火就徹底爆發了。

subtitles.en:
Then, I saw store windows smashed, and goods,
taken away.
subtitles.zh: 然後我還看到很多店面的玻璃被打碎，商品被洗劫一空。

subtitles.en: That brings us, to our third word: Looting.
subtitles.zh: 這就帶出我們今天的第三個關鍵字：趁火打劫、洗劫搶奪。

subtitles.en:
Looting. L, O, O, T, I, N, G.  How is that
different, from protesting?
subtitles.zh: 趁亂洗劫。這和正常的集會抗議有什麼不同呢？

subtitles.en:
Protesting, is fighting for rights. Looting,
is stealing.
subtitles.zh: 抗議是為了爭取權益發聲；而洗劫搶掠純粹就是犯罪偷竊。

subtitles.en:
Some people call it, "zero-dollar shopping",
online, right?
subtitles.zh: 網路上有人調侃這叫「零元購物」，對吧？

subtitles.en:
Yes. Opportunists smash windows, and steal,
expensive goods.
subtitles.zh: 是的。投機分子砸碎店家櫥窗，趁亂偷走昂貴的商品。

subtitles.en:
That really damages, local shops, and
everyday businesses.
subtitles.zh: 這對當地的商家，以及無辜做生意的老百姓，造成了很大的傷害。

subtitles.en:
Now, let's look at, the financial side, of
this story.
subtitles.zh: 現在，讓我們來看看這場風暴背後的財政問題。

subtitles.en:
France is a wealthy European country, with
very high taxes.
subtitles.zh: 法國是一個富裕的歐洲國家，而且國民繳納的稅金非常高呢。

subtitles.en:
Very high taxes, indeed. But, where does the
money go?
subtitles.zh: 確實稅收非常重。但是，那些錢到底都花去哪裡了呢？

subtitles.en:
If taxes are high, why can't schools, hire
teachers?
subtitles.zh: 既然收了那麼多稅，為什麼公立學校還會請不起老師呢？

subtitles.en:
Because, the national budget, is deep in the
red.
subtitles.zh: 因為國家的財政預算，早就深陷嚴重的赤字泥潭之中了。

subtitles.en: In the red? What does that color mean?
subtitles.zh: 身處紅色之中？這個顏色到底代表什麼意思呢？

subtitles.en:
In business accounting, red ink, represents
financial debt.
subtitles.zh: 在商業會計帳本中，紅色的墨水代表著負債與虧損。

subtitles.en: Oh! And black ink, means profit?
subtitles.zh: 噢！那黑色的墨水，就代表有盈餘賺錢囉？

subtitles.en:
Yes! "In the black", means profitable. "In
the red", means losing money.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯！身處黑色代表盈利；身處紅色則是指處於虧損赤字。

subtitles.en: How much debt, does France have, right now?
subtitles.zh: 那法國現在到底背負了多少債務啊？

subtitles.en: Over, three point six, trillion euros.
subtitles.zh: 超過三點六兆歐元。

subtitles.en:
Three point six trillion euros? That's an
astronomical number!
subtitles.zh: 三點六兆歐元？這簡直是天文數字吧！

subtitles.en:
Pensions, and public healthcare, consume huge
amounts of cash.
subtitles.zh: 龐大的退休金支出與全民健康保險，每年消耗了巨額預算。

subtitles.en:
Leaving very little budget, for schools, or
public facilities.
subtitles.zh: 結果留給學校教育或基礎公共設施的預算，就少得可憐了。

subtitles.en:
You can use this phrase, when you overspend,
too!
subtitles.zh: 當你個人消費透支超支時，也可以使用這個生動的片語喔！

subtitles.en:
Like: After holiday shopping, my bank
account, is in the red!
subtitles.zh: 就像是：放假瘋狂採購之後，我的銀行帳戶徹底見紅透支啦！

subtitles.en:
Haha, exactly! Try not to stay in the red,
for too long.
subtitles.zh: 哈哈，正是這樣！記得別讓自己的帳戶在赤字中停留太久喔。

subtitles.en:
Alex, why do French people, protest so
readily?
subtitles.zh: Alex，為什麼法國人動不動就這麼容易發起抗爭？

subtitles.en: They have, a world-famous, protest culture.
subtitles.zh: 因為他們擁有一種舉世聞名的抗爭文化。

subtitles.en:
Protest culture? Is that deeply rooted, in
their history?
subtitles.zh: 抗議文化？這是深植在他們的歷史傳統裡的嗎？

subtitles.en:
Yes. It traces all the way back, to the
French Revolution.
subtitles.zh: 是的。這一路完全可以追溯到法國大革命時期。

subtitles.en:
The storming, of the Bastille prison, in
seventeen eighty-nine!
subtitles.zh: 就是一七八九年攻佔巴士底監獄的那場歷史事件！

subtitles.en:
Exactly. French citizens believe, rights are
won, not given.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯。法國公民深信，權利是奮力爭取來的，而不是被施捨的。

subtitles.en:
They don't just sit quietly, and wait for
politicians.
subtitles.zh: 他們絕不會安靜地待在家裡，乾等政客主動帶來改變。

subtitles.en:
If train drivers are upset, trains stop
running.
subtitles.zh: 如果火車司機不滿意，全國火車立刻全面停駛。

subtitles.en:
If farmers get angry, they park tractors, on
highways!
subtitles.zh: 要是農民生氣了，他們直接把牽引機開上高速公路堵路！

subtitles.en:
Protesting, is seen as a sign, of an active
democracy.
subtitles.zh: 公開示威遊行，在他們眼中被視為民主活力的具體展現。

subtitles.en:
In many countries, people try hard, to avoid
conflict.
subtitles.zh: 在許多國家，大家大多會盡可能避免公開的正面衝突。

subtitles.en:
In France, confrontation, is brought
straight, to the streets.
subtitles.zh: 但在法國，任何衝突與歧見都會直接搬到街頭面對面交鋒。

subtitles.en:
That really shows, a completely different,
cultural mindset.
subtitles.zh: 這確實展現出一種截然不同的文化思維模式。

subtitles.en:
Looking at the news, most marchers, seemed
very young.
subtitles.zh: 看著新聞畫面，大部分上街遊行的人似乎都非常年輕呢。

subtitles.en:
Yes. Young student groups, were leading, from
the front.
subtitles.zh: 沒錯。年輕的學生族群這次帶頭衝在了最前線。

subtitles.en:
Why are young people feeling, so hopeless,
and angry?
subtitles.zh: 為什麼現在的年輕世代會感到如此無力又憤怒呢？

subtitles.en: Because of, a growing, generational divide.
subtitles.zh: 因為社會上存在著日益嚴重的世代鴻溝。

subtitles.en:
Generational divide. Divide means, a
separation, or split?
subtitles.zh: 世代鴻溝。所謂的鴻溝，是指彼此分立或隔閡的意思嗎？

subtitles.en:
Yes. A divide, between older, and younger
generations.
subtitles.zh: 是的。指的就是年長一輩與年輕世代之間巨大的處境落差。

subtitles.en:
Older generations, had steady jobs, and
affordable housing.
subtitles.zh: 老一輩當年擁有穩定的正職工作，以及負擔得起的平價房屋。

subtitles.en:
And comfortable retirement pensions, promised
by the state.
subtitles.zh: 還有國家所承諾的、能讓人安享晚年的豐厚退休金。

subtitles.en:
While young people face sky-high rents, and
temporary contracts.
subtitles.zh: 但現在的年輕人，卻面臨著高得嚇人的房租，以及毫無保障的臨時合約。

subtitles.en:
They feel, why pay heavy taxes, for a future
we won't see?
subtitles.zh: 他們心裡會想，既然我們看不到未來，又為什麼要繳納沉重的稅金呢？

subtitles.en:
That explains the sense of unfairness, behind
the riots.
subtitles.zh: 這充分說明了抗爭暴動背後，那股深深的不公與相對剝奪感。

subtitles.en:
Now, let's review, our five practical
expressions today!
subtitles.zh: 現在，讓我們一起放慢步調，複習今天學到的五個實用片語吧！

subtitles.en:
Let's repeat each phrase, slowly, and
clearly, with Alex.
subtitles.zh: 請大家跟著 Alex 一起，清楚且放慢速度地朗讀每一個片語喔。

subtitles.en: Number one: Spark a chain reaction.
subtitles.zh: 第一個：引發連鎖反應，或點燃導火線。

subtitles.en: Spark, a chain reaction.
subtitles.zh: 引發連鎖反應。

subtitles.en: Number two: At a boiling point.
subtitles.zh: 第二個：到達沸騰點，或情緒瀕臨爆發邊緣。

subtitles.en: At, a boiling point.
subtitles.zh: 到達沸騰點。

subtitles.en: Number three: Looting.
subtitles.zh: 第三個：趁火打劫，或洗劫掠奪。

subtitles.en: Looting.
subtitles.zh: 趁亂洗劫。

subtitles.en: Number four: In the red.
subtitles.zh: 第四個：陷入赤字，或處於負債虧損中。

subtitles.en: In the red.
subtitles.zh: 陷入赤字與虧損。

subtitles.en: Number five: Generational divide.
subtitles.zh: 第五個：世代隔閡，或世代斷層。

subtitles.en: Generational divide.
subtitles.zh: 世代隔閡。

subtitles.en:
Wonderful work, everyone! You did, an amazing
job.
subtitles.zh: 大家跟讀得太棒了！你們的練習表現非常出色。

subtitles.en:
And here is, our Question of the Day, for
you!
subtitles.zh: 接下來，就是我們今天為大家準備的每日互動問題時間囉！

subtitles.en:
Have you ever experienced, a strike, or
street protest, in your city?
subtitles.zh: 在你生活的城市裡，你是否曾經親身遇過罷工或街頭抗爭呢？

subtitles.en:
And which, of today's five phrases, do you
find most useful?
subtitles.zh: 而在今天所學的五個實用片語當中，你覺得哪一個對你最實用呢？

subtitles.en:
Leave a comment down below. We read, every
single one!
subtitles.zh: 歡迎在下方留言與我們分享，每一則留言我們都會認真閱讀喔！

subtitles.en:
Don't forget, to hit subscribe, and share,
with a friend.
subtitles.zh: 別忘了點擊訂閱頻道，並把這部影片分享給正在學英文的好朋友！

subtitles.en:
Speak with confidence, and we'll see you,
next time!
subtitles.zh: 帶著滿滿的自信大聲開口說英語，我們下一集再見！

subtitles.en: See you soon, everyone! Goodbye!
subtitles.zh: 大家下次見囉，掰掰！
